correctness.rationale: Any six-recovery all-symbol PIR generator forces all seven nonzero codewords to have weight >=6: choose a stored column detected by each nonzero information covector; each disjoint recovery of that target must meet the support. The binary dimension-three Griesmer bound gives n>=6+3+2=11. Independently read all 924 actual certificates.tsv rows (blob 5a9d3704278c0abefc12c0e22bcc2b0e3dff37bf) and checked in a separately implemented JS decoder that all sorted six-request multisets occur once, every target lies in the XOR span of its indicated distinct 1-based coordinates, groups are pairwise disjoint, and block-size counts are 3798 singleton/1669 pair/77 triple (5,544 groups; zero errors). Zero-target recovery follows because a span contains 0. Exhaustion is only over the finite specified six-request alphabet; the lower bound is general.

value.rationale: Simultaneous arbitrary linear-functional service is a natural strictly stronger retrieval objective than repeated-target PIR or all-symbol requests. It is mathematically informative that six arbitrary queries can be served at the classical minimum Griesmer length, using at most triples of coordinates. This exact naturally defined small parameter is a meaningful benchmark for code constructions, not a toy perturbation.

final_claim: FB(3,6,2)=ASB(3,6,2)=ASP(3,6,2)=11 for six simultaneous binary functional requests; a length-11 generator with nonzero columns 1..7 and repeats 1,2,4,7 serves all 924 nonzero request multisets with disjoint recovery sets of size <=3.
limitations: Binary dimension three and precisely six requests; no extension to higher dimension/field/t.
The explicit witness is not a uniqueness classification; priority remains best-of-knowledge.
